params.q: Up to what income is there zero income tax under the new tax regime in India?

search_parameters.q: Up to what income is there zero income tax under the new tax regime in India?

response.header: Under India’s revised new tax regime, resident individuals pay zero income tax up to ₹12,00,000, and salaried individuals effectively pay zero tax up to ₹12,75,000 due to the ₹75,000 standard deduction.

list.snippet: ₹12,00,000: Full rebate ensures no tax for any resident individual with total income up to this level under the new regime 3 .
snippet_highlighted_words: no tax for any resident individual

list.snippet: ₹12,75,000 (salaried): Because salaried taxpayers receive a standard deduction of ₹75,000, their gross income can go up to ₹12,75,000 with zero tax liability 3 .
snippet_highlighted_words: gross income can go up to ₹12,75,000

list.snippet: The Finance Minister’s Budget 2025–26 announcement states:
“There will be no income tax payable up to income of ₹12 lakh… This limit will be ₹12.75 lakh for salaried taxpayers due to standard deduction of ₹75,000.” 1
snippet_highlighted_words: no income tax payable up to income of ₹12 lakh

list.snippet: Full rebate up to ₹12,00,000, with effective no‑tax limit of ₹12,75,000 for salaried individuals 1 .
snippet_highlighted_words: effective no‑tax limit of ₹12,75,000 for salaried individuals

list.snippet: “No income tax on annual earnings up to ₹12 lakh… standard deduction raises the limit to ₹12.75 lakh.” 1
These limits apply from FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) onward under the revised new tax regime (Section 115BAC(1A)) 1 .

list.snippet: Zero tax up to ₹12 lakh for all resident individuals.
Zero tax up to ₹12.75 lakh for salaried individuals (after standard deduction).
Applies only under the new tax regime, not the old regime.

references.title: How much income is tax-free in India for AY 2026-27?
references.snippet: Under the new tax regime for AY 2026-27 (the default), income up to ₹12 lakh is effectively tax-free for resident individuals, thanks to the enhanced Section 87A rebate.

references.title: Zero Tax Up to ₹12 Lakh, 7 New Slabs, and a 30% Cap at ₹24 Lakh — The ...
references.snippet: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman confirmed in the Union Budget 2026 that the new tax slab structure — introduced under Budget 2025 — will remain intact for FY 2026-27 (Assessment Year 2027-28). The headline: zero income tax up to ₹12 lakh, seven progressive slabs, and the highest tax rate of 30% kicking in only above ₹24 lakh.

references.title: Salaried Taxpayers Get Zero Tax up to ₹12.75 Lakh - Tax Guru
references.snippet: A full rebate has been enhanced so that resident individuals pay no tax on total income up to ₹12,00,000, with marginal relief available for income slightly above this threshold. For salaried taxpayers, a standard deduction of ₹75,000 raises the effective no-tax gross income limit to ₹12,75,000.

references.title: Income Tax on Rs 12 Lakh Salary FY 2026-27: Calculation
references.snippet: Rs 12 lakh salary = zero income tax under new regime (87A rebate). Old regime costs Rs 1,63,800. Step-by-step calculation, marginal relief, and comparison.

references.title: India New Tax Regime 2026: Zero Tax on ₹12 Lakh Explained
references.snippet: For AY 2026-27, Indian residents earning up to ₹12 lakh can achieve zero tax liability through the Section 87A rebate, despite the ₹4 lakh basic exemption. Salaried individuals benefit further from a ₹75,000 standard deduction, potentially covering ₹12.75 lakh.

references.title: Marginal Relief in the New Regime (FY 2026-27): The ₹12 Lakh Cliff ...
references.snippet: In the new regime for FY 2026-27, taxable income up to ₹12 lakh pays no tax thanks to the Section 87A rebate. The moment you go even ₹1 over, the rebate vanishes.

references.title: New Tax Regime FY 2026-27: Slabs, Rebate & Benefits
references.snippet: Under Section 202 of the new Act (replacing Section 87A), taxpayers with income up to ₹12 lakh pay zero tax — the biggest relief in Indian tax history. This guide covers all new tax slabs, key changes, and whether the new regime is right for you.
